title: Growing up as girls; marriage versus school
description: Isabel Miller introduces Eva Mae Bell at her home and asks whether she was treated differently from her brothers as a girl. Patsy Larson joins, and the two women compare chores, privileges, and their decisions to marry rather than continue in school. Bell says marriage and motherhood were always her ambition and she does not regret skipping college.

title: Children; adoption during the Depression
description: Bell explains she adopted one child, a nephew, during the Depression after his parents separated, and calls raising children a woman's most worthwhile work. Larson talks about having ten pregnancies, losing two children, and wanting a large family, and both women note social pressure today against having many children.

title: Parents' objections; late schooling; wedding and shivaree
description: Bell recalls her parents' wish that she finish school and wait to marry, her late start in a one-room school, and her brother who later became a psychologist. She describes marrying a man nine years older, going to Moscow with aunts and uncles, and the shivaree back at her folks' house, with cars honking up the hill and candy and cigars passed around.

title: A lifetime in the community; clearing the farm; harvest cooperation
description: Bell says she has lived in the community 63 years and describes the stump-covered farm, the small house they built onto over time, and her husband's mill work and farming. She gives a detailed account of cooperative threshing, haying and combining, the shared machinery, and the women's rounds of cooking for fourteen or more men, rising at 4:30 and heating water on wood stoves.

title: Decline of cooperation; husbands' work; logging dangers; family size
description: The women lament the loss of cooperative harvests and the shrinking community club as farmers bought their own machinery. Larson describes her husband's well-paid but dangerous sawyering work, his injuries and her fear for him, and explains how they ended up with eight living children after infant deaths and miscarriages.

title: Health, hobbies and Sunday school; raising boys and girls
description: Bell talks about being rockhounds, her heart failure and asthma, and her 23 years of Sunday school teaching which she loves. Larson describes art classes and school volunteering, and the women compare raising boys and girls, sons with dolls and teddy bears, daughters' careers and futures, and end with how the couple makes decisions together.
